faq: What does this tool calculate?
The zoom satisfying m/px = 156,543.03 × cos(lat) ÷ 2^zoom, solved for zoom — reported fractionally, with the neighbouring integer zooms' resolutions for context.
Which map standard does it use?
The slippy-map standard (Web Mercator, 256-px tiles) shared by OSM, Google and MapLibre.
Can I use this in production GIS?
The formulas are the production standard itself — yes for web-mapping work.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — tile systems are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — tiles and pixels quantise; decimals beyond the cell are decoration.
Why fractional zooms?
Resolution is continuous; integer zooms are a tiling convenience. The true match is fractional — libraries with fractional zoom render it natively.
Imagery resolution versus display?
A dataset's native resolution is its information content; display zoom is presentation. Matching them avoids both blur and empty zoom — this page is the match.
DPI-based data?
Scanned maps quote DPI at a print scale — convert to ground resolution first (scale ÷ DPI maths), then to zoom.
Higher latitude helps?
The same zoom resolves finer ground poleward, so a resolution matches a higher zoom — the calculator's latitude input carries the effect.
Max native zoom for tiles?
Set it at the resolution's ceiling (floor of the fractional zoom) — deeper tiles are upsampling wearing a uniform.
